title: Design the acre language
body: What an `.acre` file looks like: how it declares the canvas and the objects on it, and later how each object changes over time. Jack settles the syntax by writing files in a working version and reacting to them. Each version goes into `crates/acre/src/lang` and `scene` once it is small enough to try. Over those versions, pin down the top-level shape of a file, how time is written (seconds, frames, or both), and how a property is animated between two values.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/89ec73b0
notes.text: Settled so far, syntax still open: canvas coordinates are pixels with the origin top-left. Time is seconds in the model; the frame index belongs to the renderer. The domain is arrays, matrices, grids and simple plots, so text in cells and on axes is in the first version. First examples to design the syntax against: an array of numbers being sorted (highlight the compared pair, swap them) and a line plot that draws itself with points appearing.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/89ed765a
notes.text:
Jack wants joined editing in the acre GUI. The GUI holds a text editor beside the render. Editing the text re-renders the scene. Dragging or stretching an object in the render rewrites the source text. To support that, `lang` and `scene` need four things:

- a parser that keeps comments and whitespace, so acre can rewrite one literal and leave the rest of the file as typed
- the source span of every value in the scene
- an id on every scene object that carries through to the primitives it draws
- a way for `scene` to say which object is under a point on the canvas

A value computed from other values has no single literal to rewrite. A grid cell whose x comes from its index is one. The syntax design has to say what a drag does to such a value. Two options so far are to refuse the drag, or to rewrite the nearest literal that feeds it, such as the grid's origin. Neither is chosen.

Static images, diagrams and plots are the main use. Simple animations still matter.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/89ed765a
notes.text:
Jack can't judge a syntax on paper. He wants a language he can run and react to, with still images settled before animation. The syntax uses braces and should look nothing like Python.

v0 is the first version to play with. A file is a tree of nodes. A node is a kind, an optional name and a braced body of properties (`key values;`) and child nodes. The parser gives nothing a meaning. `scene` interprets each node kind, so a change of vocabulary leaves the parser alone. The node kinds in v0 are `canvas`, `box`, `ellipse`, `line`, `arrow` and `text`. v0 has no time.

Three earlier candidates are set aside until still images work. They were objects plus a timeline, inline keyframes on every property, and sequenced steps.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/89ed765a
notes.text: v0 landed in f5a9de6. `crates/acre/examples/layers.acre` is its first example file.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/cd2d1020
notes.text:
v1 adds the nodes the `PrefixEncoder` figure (acre-de907c) needed. Nothing in it is committed yet.

| node or property | what it does | why |
|---|---|---|
| `row` | cells on a grid of equal units, each covering a whole number of units | a 64-bit word is 21 cells of 3 bits and one of 1, so a cell's width has to follow its bits |
| `cells "G" "A" ...;` and `cell { ... }` children | the list covers the common case, and a child cell overrides span, fill, stroke or note | 21 cells written as nodes would be 21 lines per row |
| `palette NAME { symbol "A" #color "001"; }` | fills and notes by cell text | each character keeps one colour and its code across every row |
| `brace` with `over ROW A B` | a curly or square bracket along cells A to B | the figure labels runs of cells, and computing their pixels by hand would break when a row moves |
| `ruler` | a numbered scale of units | bit numbers from 63 down to 0 under a key |
| `from ROW N side` on `line` and `arrow` | ends a line at a cell, or at the middle of one of its sides | the roll panel joins cell k of one row to cell k-1 of the next |
| `font` on the canvas and on any text | `mono`, `sans`, `sans-bold`, `sans-italic` | prose in Noto Sans, code names in monospace |
| `dash`, `radius`, `\n` in strings | dashed strokes, rounded boxes, multi-line text | |

The example the PrefixEncoder figure, which never went into git came from a script that computed the keys and coordinates. Writing the file by hand would mean placing about 300 objects with numbers worked out on paper. The language has no arithmetic, loops or relative placement, and those three are what a hand-written figure of this size would need.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/cd2d1020
notes.text:
v2 makes a figure the size of the `PrefixEncoder` one writable by hand. the PrefixEncoder figure, which never went into git is now hand-written in 171 lines. The generated version was 229 lines of absolute coordinates.

- `let NAME VALUES;` on the canvas. A bare word equal to a let name stands for its values in any property. The substitution runs before `scene` reads a node, in `scene/expand.rs`. It has no scoping, so a let name shadows any word value of the same spelling, such as `right` or `show`.
- `style NAME { ... }` and `style A B;` on a node. A node's own property wins over a style's, and a later style over an earlier one. Styles reach nested nodes such as a row's `cell` children.
- `group { at X Y; ... }` moves the numbers in every `at`, `from` and `to` inside it. Names stay global, and an end that names a thing uses where that thing already is.
- `at NAME DX DY` starts from a shape's or a row's top-left corner, and `at ROW N DX DY` from a cell's. A row name followed by exactly one number reads as a cell, so `at row -60 14` has to give both numbers.
- `chars "GATC"` adds a cell per character.
- `repeat N` on `line` and `arrow` draws N copies, adding one to every cell index on each copy. The 20 lines of the roll panel are one node.
- A palette `symbol` takes a text color after its note, for white text on dark cells.

The derived-values box still takes 15 `text` nodes for a three-column table. A `table` node, or text that mixes colours within a line, would shorten it. Neither is built.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/cd2d1020
notes.text:
v3 adds arithmetic, markup in text and a `table` node. the PrefixEncoder figure, which never went into git is now 160 lines with no number worked out by hand.

- `(a + b * c)` is a number. The parser keeps a parenthesized run as a group, and `scene/expand.rs` evaluates it after it substitutes `let` names, so `let u 15;` and `at key (64 * u + 76) 8` work. `-` between terms needs spaces, because `a-b` lexes as one word and `-1` as a number. A negative number straight after a term reads as subtraction, so `(x -1)` is `x - 1`.
- Markup in every label: `` `code` `` for mono, `**bold**`, `{NAME text}` for a `let` color, `{#rrggbb text}`. A `Label` and `Primitive::Text` now hold runs of font and color, and the renderer lays a line out across runs. The figure uses it for every code name in prose and for the coloured formula in the roll panel.
- `table { at; columns X...; align ...; row "a" "b" "c"; ... }` lowers to one text per cell. The derived-values box went from 15 nodes to one.
- `let left 230` broke `align left`, as the v2 note warned. A `let` name may no longer be one of the words properties read as they are (`left`, `right`, `top`, `bottom`, `center`, `none`, `show`, `hide`, `curly`, `square` and the font names). That list sits in `RESERVED` in `scene/expand.rs` and has to grow with the vocabulary.

Open: mono text inside a bold title is set in regular weight, since acre embeds no bold mono face. The markup has no italic mark.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/ed2a7ee0
notes.text:
Canvas `size` takes `auto` for either side (acre-abc054, commit below on dev).

- `size 1900 auto` fixes the width. `size auto auto` fixes neither. `size auto 800` also works, since each side is read on its own.
- An `auto` side is the box around everything drawn, measured by the same code as `Scene::bounds`, plus `margin` on both ends. The scene is built once to measure and once more shifted so the drawing starts at the margin on each `auto` axis. A fixed side is not shifted.
- `margin N` is one number on the canvas, default 20. One number keeps it as small as the plan allows. A default of 0 would leave text touching the edge of the image. 20 matches the padding most figures give their panels.
- `margin` on a canvas with no `auto` is an error, because it would be ignored otherwise.
- Bounds are taken at time 0 only, which is all the language has today. Revisit when animation lands.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/ed2a7ee0
notes.text:
Math syntax, from acre-3f9f94 (commits 7f31032 to 070e175 on dev).

- `$...$` in any label's markup is a formula in LaTeX math. `$` always opens one, and `\$` is a dollar sign. A `$` with no partner is an error that tells the writer to use `\$`. I rejected a rule that guesses from context, as pandoc does (no space after the opening `$`, no digit after the closing one). It lets most lone dollars through, but a label would change meaning when someone adds a second `$` to it. The error catches every case at build time instead. In DNA figures the `$` sits in row cells, `chars` and palette symbols, which take no markup, so `figures/key-schemes.acre` builds unchanged.
- Inside `$...$` in a quoted string, the lexer keeps every backslash with the character after it. Otherwise `$\nu$` would read `\n` as a line break, and `\frac` would be an unknown escape. The lexer already kept `\{`, `\}`, `` \` `` and `\*` for markup, and now also knows `$`.
- `math { at; text """FORMULA"""; size; color; align; }` sets one formula in display style, placed by its top edge like `text`. Its formula has no `$` signs, so in a quoted string `\frac` would need `\\frac`. A `"""` string takes no escapes and is the form to write. The node builds a `Text` whose one run, in `Font::Math`, is `\displaystyle` followed by the formula.
- `\displaystyle`, `\textstyle`, `\scriptstyle` and `\scriptscriptstyle` work anywhere in a formula, so inline math can ask for display style.
- An unknown command is an error, not text. The subset is the tables `GREEK`, `SYMBOLS`, `LARGE_OPS` and `OPERATOR_NAMES` in `crates/acre/src/math/parse.rs`, plus `\frac`, `\sqrt`, `\left`, `\right`, `\text`, `\mathrm`, `\operatorname`, `\limits`, `\nolimits` and the spaces `\,`, `\:`, `\;`, `\!`, `\quad`, `\qquad`.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/ed2a7ee0
notes.text:
Syntax chosen for connectors.

- `route straight | elbow | curve`. An elbow has three segments and turns halfway along the longer of the two distances between the ends. A curve is a cubic whose handles run along that same axis, so it leaves and arrives like the elbow does. It is drawn as 24 straight segments.
- `head` and `tail` take `none | triangle | open | dot`. An `arrow` defaults to a triangle head and a `line` to none, so existing files draw as before.
- `label-side above | left | right` and `label-at F`, two properties. A single property such as `label left 0.3` would mix a word and a number. `left` and `right` are as seen going from `from` to `to`, so they flip when the ends swap. `above` is the default: the normal that faces up, or right on a vertical line. On a horizontal line it is the old position.
- The label's box is measured with the text layout and centered on the normal at `gap + half its extent along the normal`. Descenders are ignored when measuring the bottom, which keeps a horizontal line's label where it was.

Not done: routing around shapes in the way. Elbow and curve use only the two ends.
